title: Aluwa (Sri Lankan rice-flour fudge)
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the water over medium heat and cook until it forms a thick syrup that holds a thread between two fingers.
Stir in the rice flour, cashews and cardamom quickly and keep stirring until the mixture is a thick, stiff dough.
Pour onto a greased tray and press flat to about 1.5 cm thick.
Cool for a few minutes, then cut into diamond shapes with a greased knife.
Let them set completely before serving.

title: Athirasa (Sri Lankan jaggery rice-flour fried cakes)
steps: Dissolve the jaggery in the water over low heat and bring to a gentle boil until it thickens a little.
Gradually stir in the rice flour, coconut, cardamom and salt, forming a thick, sticky dough.
Cool the dough until you can handle it, then shape into flat discs about 6 cm wide.
Fry in medium-hot oil until deep brown on both sides.
Drain on paper and cool before serving.

title: Bibikkan (Sri Lankan coconut jaggery cake)
steps: Heat the oven to 160 C and grease a baking tin.
Cream the ghee with the jaggery, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Mix in the coconut, semolina, flour, spices, salt and cashews.
Spread the batter in the tin and bake for 45 to 50 minutes until firm and a deep brown.
Cool in the tin and cut into squares.

title: Idiyappam (Sri Lankan string hoppers)

ingredients.name: coconut sambol and dhal curry to serve

steps: Mix the rice flour and salt in a bowl and stir in the boiling water and oil until a soft, smooth dough forms; cool slightly.
Knead it while still warm until pliable.
Fill an idiyappam press (or a piping bag with a star nozzle) with some dough.
Press the dough in small spirals onto oiled idli moulds or small squares of banana leaf.
Steam for 6 to 8 minutes until they are cooked and no longer sticky.
Serve warm with pol sambol, dhal curry or fish curry.

title: Jaffna Crab Curry (Sri Lankan roasted-spice crab curry)

ingredients.name: whole crabs, cleaned and cut into pieces

steps: Heat the oil in a wide pot and fry the onion, garlic, ginger and curry leaves until golden.
Stir in the curry powder, chilli powder, turmeric and pepper and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the crab pieces and toss to coat in the spices.
Pour in the water, tamarind and salt, cover and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until the shells turn bright red and the crab is cooked.
Add the coconut milk and simmer uncovered for 5 more minutes until the gravy thickens.
Serve with rice, pittu or bread.

title: Kalu Dodol (Sri Lankan black coconut-jaggery toffee)

ingredients.name: kithul or palm jaggery (or dark jaggery), grated

steps: Whisk the rice flour with a little of the coconut milk until smooth, then mix in the rest of the coconut milk.
Add the jaggery, sugar and salt and stir until dissolved.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for about 1 to 1.5 hours until the mixture turns dark, glossy and very thick and pulls away from the pan.
Stir in the cashews and cardamom and pour into a greased tray.
Let it cool completely, then cut into small squares.

title: Kevum (Sri Lankan oil cake)
steps: Melt the jaggery in the water over low heat, strain to remove impurities and cool until warm.
Mix the rice flour and salt with the jaggery syrup and coconut milk to a thick batter.
Let the batter rest for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep pan to medium-hot.
Drop a ladle of batter into the oil, letting it spread and form a ring shape with a raised centre, and fry until deep golden.
Drain on paper and serve at room temperature.

title: Kiri Aluwa (Sri Lankan milk toffee)
steps: Mix the sugar and water in a pan and boil until it forms a light syrup.
Stir in the condensed milk and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick.
Add the milk powder, cardamom and cashews and mix until a stiff paste forms.
Pour into a buttered tray and level the surface.
Cool for 20 minutes and cut into diamonds or squares.

title: Kiribath (Sri Lankan milk rice)

ingredients.name: lunu miris or seeni sambol, to serve

steps: Cook the rice in the water with the salt until it is very soft and the water is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and cook over low heat for another 10 minutes, stirring, until the rice is creamy and sticky.
Spread the rice in a greased tray or plate and press it flat to a thickness of about 2.5 cm.
Cool for 10 minutes, then cut into diamonds or squares.
Serve warm with lunu miris, seeni sambol or banana.

title: Kokis (Sri Lankan crispy rice-flour and coconut milk cookies)
steps: Whisk the rice flour, coconut milk, egg, salt and sugar into a smooth thick batter and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep pan to medium-hot and warm the kokis mould in the oil.
Dip the hot mould in the batter without covering the top of the mould.
Lower it into the oil and shake until the batter shape slides off, then fry until golden.
Drain on paper and cool; they crisp as they cool.

title: Kola Kanda (Sri Lankan green leaf rice porridge)

ingredients.name: gotu kola or spinach leaves, blended with 1/2 cup water and strained

steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it in the water with the garlic until very soft and broken down, about 30 minutes.
Stir in the strained green leaf juice and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and salt and simmer gently for another 5 minutes without letting it boil hard.
Serve warm in bowls, topped with a spoon of grated coconut and a piece of jaggery on the side if you like.

title: Kottu Roti (Sri Lankan chopped flatbread stir-fry)

ingredients.name: roti or parathas, shredded into strips (or 4 flour tortillas)

steps: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil, fry the chicken with the curry powder and salt until cooked through, then set aside.
In the same pan heat the remaining oil and fry the onion, garlic, ginger, chillies and curry leaves until fragrant.
Add the carrot and cabbage and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then push everything aside and scramble the eggs in the clear space.
Add the chicken, shredded roti, chilli powder, turmeric and a splash of water or gravy.
Stir-fry on high heat while chopping the roti with two metal spatulas until it is mixed with everything and slightly crisp at the edges.
Serve immediately with a spicy curry sauce on the side.

title: Lamprais (Dutch-Burgher rice and curry parcel)

ingredients.name: banana leaves, wilted over a flame

steps: Cook the rice in the stock with the salt and a pinch of cinnamon until tender and the stock is absorbed.
Fry the onion in the oil, add the chicken, curry powder and salt, add a little water and simmer until the chicken is cooked and the sauce is thick.
Fry the aubergine slices until golden and prepare the sambol.
Place a portion of rice on each banana leaf, then add some chicken curry, an egg half, aubergine and a spoon of sambol.
Fold the leaf into a parcel and tie it with kitchen string.
Bake at 180 C for 20 minutes until the leaf has darkened and the flavours have melded; open at the table.

title: Lunu Miris (Sri Lankan chilli and onion paste)
steps: Mash the chilli, salt and Maldive fish together in a mortar until well mixed.
Add the chopped onion and crush it lightly so it releases some juice.
Stir in the lime juice and oil and let the paste rest for 10 minutes.
Serve with kiribath, pol roti or rice.

title: Mallung (Sri Lankan greens with coconut)

ingredients.name: kale, spinach or gotu kola, very finely shredded

steps: Heat the oil in a pan and splutter the mustard seeds with the curry leaves.
Add the onion and chillies and cook until soft.
Stir in the turmeric and greens and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until just wilted.
Add the coconut and salt and toss for another 2 minutes, then finish with lime juice.
Serve warm as a side to rice and curry.

title: Parippu (Sri Lankan red lentil curry with coconut milk)
steps: Put the lentils, water, turmeric, half the onion, chillies, curry leaves and pandan in a pot and boil.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the lentils are very soft, stirring now and then.
Add the salt and coconut milk and stir over low heat for 5 minutes without boiling hard.
Heat the oil in a small pan, fry the mustard seeds, remaining onion and dried chilli until browned.
Pour the tempering over the dhal and serve with rice or roti.

title: Pittu (Sri Lankan steamed rice flour and coconut cylinders)

ingredients.name: coconut milk and sambol or curry to serve

steps: Mix the rice flour and salt in a bowl and sprinkle in warm water a little at a time, rubbing it with your fingertips until the flour holds together in crumbs when squeezed.
Rub the crumbs through a coarse sieve for an even, loose texture.
Layer the flour and coconut alternately in a pittu steamer or a tall steamer basket, starting and ending with coconut.
Steam for 8 to 10 minutes until steam comes through the top layer.
Push out the cylinder and serve warm with coconut milk, sambol or a curry.

title: Pol Sambol (Sri Lankan coconut sambal)

ingredients.name: red chilli powder (or 3 fresh red chillies)

steps: Pound or mash the onion with the chilli powder, salt and Maldive fish with a mortar or the back of a spoon until it forms a rough paste.
Add the grated coconut and pepper and work together with your fingers until the coconut turns pale red.
Stir in the lime juice and adjust salt and heat.
Serve fresh with hoppers, bread, kiribath or rice and curry.

source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Seeni Sambol (Sri Lankan caramelised onion relish)
steps: Fry the onions in the oil on medium heat with the curry leaves, lemongrass, cinnamon and cloves until soft and starting to brown, about 15 minutes.
Add the chilli powder, salt, sugar and tamarind pulp and keep cooking on low heat for another 15 to 20 minutes, stirring, until the onions are dark and jammy.
Stir in the Maldive fish if using and cook for 2 more minutes.
Serve at room temperature with bread, kiribath or rice.

title: Thala Guli (Sri Lankan sesame and jaggery balls)

ingredients.name: white or black sesame seeds, toasted

steps: Boil the jaggery with the water until it forms a thick syrup, about 5 minutes.
Add the toasted sesame seeds, cardamom and coconut, if using, and stir for 2 to 3 minutes.
Remove from the heat and, while the mixture is still warm, take small portions with greased hands.
Press and roll each into a ball and set on a plate.
Let them harden for 30 minutes before serving.

title: Watalappam (Sri Lankan coconut custard pudding)
steps: Dissolve the jaggery in the coconut milk over low heat, then cool slightly.
Beat the eggs lightly with the spices and salt and mix in the coconut milk mixture.
Strain the custard into a heatproof dish, scatter the cashews on top and cover tightly with foil.
Steam over simmering water, or bake in a water bath at 160 C, for 35 to 40 minutes until set.
Cool and chill before serving.
